title: Deadly Poisonous Spider Trap
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, the Detective Boys, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Takagi, the Inspector) omitted by convention, matching ep011. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: accidental_death_by_staged_scare (the victim was never actually envenomated -- he died of a stress-induced heart attack after believing he'd been bitten). The old low-fidelity case file (cases/ep373...) got the culprit right (Miwa Yasuda) and the core mechanism right (staged bite via a dead spider on a hidden needle, missing antivenom), but it under-modeled the case: it had no node for the needle/thumb-tack itself, missed Itokawa's cover-up (pocketing Yasuda's dropped nail-art decal), missed the matching-cellphone evidence that exposed the Itokawa/Yasuda relationship (and thus Yasuda's access to a copied spare key), and generically 'knows' every suspect to the victim instead of the real motive/relationship structure (Itokawa is Nino's research assistant whose work Nino was stealing credit for; Urasaki is a recent acquaintance Nino pressured into selling him rare spiders; Yasuda is Itokawa's girlfriend acting to protect him). Transcript confirms the culprit acted without intent to kill -- she expected the professor to merely be hospitalized -- which the old file's motive_type already captured correctly.

clues.desc: The spider was already dead before contact, and the needle it sat on had a broken, invisible tip -- together they prove the 'bite' was staged, not a real envenomation.
Autopsy shows no venom entered Nino's body; cause of death was a stress-induced heart attack from panicking over the missing antivenom, not the spider itself.
Itokawa's and Yasuda's cellphones are the same rare model in different colors, and both antennas carry matching scratches -- proving they're a couple and one antenna snapped the needle's tip.
The blue flower nail-art decal pocketed by Itokawa matches the decal visible on Yasuda's nails in her own magazine photo -- ties the dropped decal directly to her presence at the scene.

edges.motive_type: resentment_over_stolen_research_credit (red herring -- Itokawa is one of only two normal keyholders, making him look guilty)

edges.detail: gets Urasaki to be the one who calls Nino, so neither she nor Itokawa is the traceable caller

edges.method: staged fake spider bite induced a panic-driven fatal heart attack when the antivenom could not be found
